objective: Measure S2's rebalance timing luck across 21 monthly signal-day offsets, mirroring H-20260928-01's S3 check, so the paper renewal and any future live-pilot sizing use a date-neutral expectation. Purely descriptive: no offset is adopted.
target_regime_and_horizon: Same regime S2 is already paper-traded under: US ETF rotation momentum. Stress/select/anchor/holdout windows identical to H-20260928-01 (S1 stress from 2017-01-03 for its 252-session lookback). The live rule is frozen; this result only sets renewal/sizing expectations.
existing_solution_comparison: H-20260928-01 already surveyed rebalance-timing-luck literature (Hoffstein/Faber/Braun, Concretum 2025, CXO Advisory, Allocate Smartly) and ran the identical 21-offset descriptive check on S3 using the frozen salvage engine. `oc research directions check` confirms dir:s3_rebalance_timing_luck_tranching is the only prior local test; nothing existing covers S1 or S2 specifically, so the only missing piece is running the same already-validated method on these two sleeves. No new mechanism to research.
remaining_evidence_gap: Whether S2's own headline anchor/select numbers, like S3's, sit near the best of its own offset distribution (a lucky rebalance date) or are closer to the median.
negative_experiments_checked: H-20260928-01 (dir:s3_rebalance_timing_luck_tranching, refuted 0/4 for tranching, but established that S3's month-end anchor CAGR/Sharpe was the best of 21 offsets): the descriptive offset-distribution method itself was not refuted, only the T4 tranching adoption rule. This round reuses the descriptive method only, no tranching, on S1/S2.
cost_and_execution_assumptions: Frozen engine: scripts/run_h20260922_05_salvage.py sleeve_weights/run_cell, signal at close, fill next open, 10 bp per side primary, 20 bp stress. No new cost assumption.
stop_condition: None -- this is a purely descriptive measurement (min/median/max/live-rank), not an adoption test; there is no pass/fail bar and no offset is adopted regardless of the result.

sources.claim: In a concentrated (20-stock) monthly-rebalanced US momentum portfolio, 1991-2024, the CAGR gap between the best and worst trading day of the month was 348 bp; splitting into 2-20 tranches left the mean CAGR (16.7-16.8%) and Sharpe (0.59-0.60) unchanged while shrinking the dispersion from 3.48% to 0-2%. Single-day max drawdowns ranged -69.3% to -74.9%.
